frequency_question: How often have major bilateral administrative/water resource treaties been successfully drafted, reviewed, and signed within a 49-day calendar window given standard bureaucratic sequencing?
membership_rule: Includes formal transboundary water or major resource agreements requiring inter-ministerial clearance, legal vetting, and executive sign-off. Excluded: informal verbal understandings, purely domestic regulations, or treaties with infinite open-ended negotiation horizons.

skeleton: Sequential bureaucratic phases: Inter-ministerial drafting (30 days) + Legal vetting by Ministry of Law (15 days) + Cabinet/Executive approval (14 days) + Formal signing ceremony preparation (10 days). Total minimum sequential time = 69 days.
multiplier: 69 days required minimum vs 49 days available window
validity_reason: Bureaucratic procedures and inter-ministerial clearance workflows in South Asian federal administrations remain structurally consistent over multi-year periods.
